answer: In a decentralized consensus network, a Sybil-resistant mechanism is reputation-based proof-of-stake, where validators must "stake" a pearl of valuable cryptocurrency to participate. An attacker attempting to create multiple fake identities would need to acquire and lock up a corresponding amount of cryptocurrency for each, a costly endeavor akin to building an artificial knoll. Validators are incentivized to maintain a good reputation, as a malicious actor would be ejected from the network and forfeit their staked assets, which are then deposited into a community-controlled harbor fund.
